title: Your Big Stock Trades Just Got Bigger: Understanding Block Deals
description: Block deals are special, large share transactions done by big investors. They happen in separate, short trading windows on stock exchanges.

faq.q: Who regulates block deals in India?
faq.a: Block deals in India are regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to ensure transparency, fairness, and market integrity.

faq.q: Can I, as a small investor, participate in a block deal?
faq.a: No, small retail investors cannot directly participate in block deals because they have a high minimum transaction value, currently set at ₹25 crore, making them exclusive to large institutional investors.

faq.q: What are the specific timings for block deals on stock exchanges?
faq.a: Block deals are executed during two specific windows: a morning window, typically from 8:45 AM to 9:00 AM, and an afternoon window, usually from 2:05 PM to 2:20 PM.

faq.q: What does the "100% delivery" mandate for block deals mean?
faq.a: It means that for every block deal, the shares bought must be physically delivered and cannot be squared off (sold back) within the same trading day, ensuring genuine change of ownership.

faq.q: Why did SEBI increase the minimum value for block deals?
faq.a: SEBI increased the minimum value to ensure that the block deal window is used for genuine, high-conviction, large-scale investment and divestment decisions, preventing its misuse for smaller, speculative trades and enhancing market integrity.
